## Process error worth recording

My Bash cwd was the **main checkout** (`/Users/ylpromax5/Workspace/Kaola-Workflow`), not the worktree
— the two share a HEAD (`fa5157b3`) so relative-path greps read identical tracked content and nothing
looked wrong. One line-splice ran on a relative path and deleted 92 lines from
`/Users/ylpromax5/Workspace/Kaola-Workflow/scripts/test-release.js`. Restored immediately with
`git show HEAD:scripts/test-release.js > <path>` (not `git checkout --`); `git status` in the main
checkout is clean apart from this note folder. Every subsequent read, write and sweep used absolute
worktree paths, and every "orphaned" claim below was re-verified against the **worktree** afterwards.

## TASK A — issue #888: the release-prep carry-over, deleted

### What was deleted, and the evidence each was carry-over-only

**`scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js`** (canonical anchor; the ×3 copies are un-propagated —
see *Propagation debt*):

| symbol | lines (pre-edit) | evidence it was carry-over-only |
|---|---|---|
| `evaluateReleasePrepCarryOver` | 1507-1570 (64) | one call site in the whole tree: `evaluateReleaseReceipt` :1649. Not exported (export block read in full). |
| `firstJsonDifference` | 1481-1505 (25) | called only from `evaluateReleasePrepCarryOver` :1562 and its own two recursions. Not exported. |
| `RELEASE_VERSIONED_JSON_FILES` | 1477-1479 (3) | read only at `evaluateReleasePrepCarryOver` :1549. Not exported. |
| the `else` arm of the binding block | 1644-1655 | `let binding` / `let carryOver` existed only to name which of two routes bound. |
| `binding` + `carryOver` on the pass envelope | 1707-1709 | see *The `binding` field* below. |

Replaced the binding block with a direct refusal: `stamped !== candidate` →
`attachChainsStaleDiagnostics(refuseWith('chains_stale', …))`. Comment blocks at the `RELEASE_FILES`
definition, the `evaluateReleaseReceipt` header and the returns-contract line were rewritten to
describe strict equality only, naming #888's measurement as the reason.

**`scripts/kaola-workflow-run-chains.js`** — `runReleaseCheck`: deleted `binding`, `carryOver`,
`routeText` and the `Object.assign` that spliced them into the JSON envelope; the human line drops
`; bound by strict sha equality`. Header comment rewritten.

**`scripts/kaola-workflow-release.js`**:

- `receiptBindsTo` (whole function, :148-151) — **deleted**. Its body was
  `verdict.ok || !(verdict.carryOver && verdict.carryOver.failed)`. With `carryOver` gone that
  expression is `verdict.ok || true` — i.e. always `true`, which would have made the surrounding
  `chains_stale` arm in `chainReceiptGreenness` unreachable. Deleting the helper and its `&&` clause
  restores line 143 of the pre-#881 file **byte-for-byte** (verified with
  `git show 523f1241^:scripts/kaola-workflow-release.js`; 523f1241 is the commit that introduced
  `receiptBindsTo`). This is the one place where "delete the mechanism" was not a pure subtraction,
  and getting it wrong would have silently disarmed `--verify`'s staleness warning.
- `chainCheck` :245 — `verdict.carryOver ? verdict.carryOver.receiptSha : verdict.candidate` →
  `verdict.candidate`. The delegation to `evaluateReleaseReceipt` itself is **kept**: it is #881's
  "one binding rule, one implementation" half, not the carry-over.
- `--prepare`'s human line no longer says a receipt "carries over that commit"; it now says to run
  the offline full chain at that commit.

**Forge ports** — `plugins/kaola-workflow-{gitea,gitlab}/scripts/kaola-{gitea,gitlab}-workflow-{run-chains,release}.js`.
Correction to the brief: these are **not** hand-maintained. `scripts/edition-sync.js`
`GENERATED_AGGREGATORS` (:52-65) lists `kaola-workflow-run-chains.js` and `kaola-workflow-release.js`,
and `--check` renders each through `renderForgePort(canon, base, forge)` and compares. Hand-editing
them would have to reproduce the render byte-for-byte. So I ran the repo's own exported
`renderForgePort` against the edited canonical and wrote exactly those four paths — the same bytes
`--write` produces, without touching any other plugin file. `edition-sync.js --check` is green.

### The `binding` field — a public envelope key, removed

`--release-check --json` no longer emits `binding` (nor the `carryOver` sibling). It had exactly two
possible values and existed only to say which of the two routes bound; with one route it is a
constant. Load-bearing evidence that this is a restoration rather than a break: **`docs/api.md` :411
already documents the pass envelope as** `{ "result": "pass", "mode": "release-check", "candidate":
"<sha>", "chains": [] }` — #881 added `binding` to the code and never updated the documented shape.
Removing it makes code and doc agree again. Flagging it anyway because it is a JSON contract key.

### What was deliberately KEPT

- **Exact-`headSha` binding is enforced by `evaluateReleaseReceipt` itself**, in the anchor: after
  the `stamped`/`unknown` check and the unresolved-candidate check, `if (stamped !== candidate)`
  returns `chains_stale`. That single comparison is now the whole binding rule, and both entry
  points (`run-chains.js --release-check` and `release.js --tag` via `chainCheck`) call that one
  function, so they still cannot answer differently.
- The four-chain demand, coverage check, waiver refusal, dirty-stamp refusal, `repo_kind_undetermined`
  fail-closed and the typed precedence family — all untouched.
- `RELEASE_FILES`, `CODEX_MANIFEST_RELPATHS`, `CLAUDE_MANIFEST_RELPATHS` — live: `release.js`
  `--prepare` reads `RELEASE_FILES` at 6 sites in every edition. Only the carry-over's *use* of it
  went.
- `attachChainsStaleDiagnostics` / `stale_paths` / `stale_kind` — live and still attached on the
  mismatch arm.
- `chainCheck`'s delegation to the kernel (#881's non-carry-over half).

### Docs

- `docs/conventions.md` — the pre-tag-gate bullet, the `chains_stale` precedence gloss, the
  **Working sequence** bullet, the `--tag` bullet and the *Relationship to `--release-check`*
  paragraph. The working sequence now names the four-chain run at the release commit as a mandatory
  step and records *why* the carry-over went: the sink's `chore: archive <project>` commit puts
  `kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/**` between the finishing receipt and the release commit, those
  paths are off-surface by construction, and the workflow has no release path avoiding the sink.
  Stated as an unreachable branch that was deleted rather than widened — no claim that anything is
  saved. The #890 changelog-reference bullet was **not** touched.
- `docs/api.md` — the `--release-check` binding bullet. The envelope example at :411 needed no edit
  (see *The `binding` field*).

### Not touched, deliberately

`CHANGELOG.md` — a `changelog-draft-2` agent is on this run and `[Unreleased]` already carries a
`### Removed` section. Suggested entry, for whoever owns it:

> **The release-prep carry-over is deleted; the four-chain run at the release commit is mandatory
> (#888).** #881 let a receipt stamped at an ancestor of the release candidate bind when the
> intervening diff stayed inside `RELEASE_FILES`. Cutting v9.0.0 measured that it cannot fire: the
> sink writes `chore: archive <project>`, whose entire content is `kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/**`,
> and that commit always interposes in the only release sequence the workflow has — so the route
> refused `off_surface` every time. Gone with it: `evaluateReleasePrepCarryOver`,
> `firstJsonDifference`, `RELEASE_VERSIONED_JSON_FILES`, `release.js`'s `receiptBindsTo`, and the
> `binding` / `carryOver` keys on the `--release-check` pass envelope (which `docs/api.md` had never
> documented). `--release-check` binds by exact `headSha` equality and nothing else; the four-chain,
> unwaived, clean-stamp demand is unchanged.

## TASK B — issue #894 site 2: the curated-root vocabulary, deleted

Deleted from `scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js`: `CURATED_ROOT_PATHS` (:435-443),
`CURATED_ROOT_LC` (:451), `extractCuratedRootPaths` (:463-476), their three comment blocks
(:426-434, :444-450, :452-462), and the export at :1778. 51 lines + 1 export line.

**Verified by reading, not by grep.** The local `grep` is ugrep and skips dot-directories, so I wrote
a `fs.readdirSync` walker that descends every directory except `.git` and `node_modules` and reports
every matching line. It swept **8697 files across 892 directories** of the worktree. `.opencode*` and
`.kimi*` do not exist in this repo at all — `git ls-files | grep -c '^\.opencode\|^\.kimi'` = 0, and
the only top-level dot-entries are `.agents`, `.env.example`, `.git`, `.gitignore` (`.agents` swept
and clean). After the canonical deletion the three symbols survive **only** in the three
un-propagated anchor copies and in `CHANGELOG.md` release history (:2259-2260, historical prose about
v3.21.0 — correctly left alone). Zero consumers.

Consistent with the #891 run's own record: `kaola-workflow/archive/issue-891/mission-list.md` :34
states the symbol "lost its last caller" and was left in place only because the anchor is a four-copy
change.
